# Settings reference

<!-- generated by tools/gen_settings_doc.py - do not edit by hand -->

Every setting below can be changed in the web UI under **Settings** (and **Companies**). Changes are stored in the database, apply immediately and are shared by the web app and the command-line scraper. Each page has *Reset to defaults*. The *Path* column is the key you can also use in `config.yaml`.

## Profile & motivation letters

Your details fill the copy-paste snippets. The rest is the raw material for the motivation letter on every job page: the more of your own facts it has, the more personal and specific each letter is. Skills also drive the match score.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Full name | `profile.name` | *(empty)* |  |
| Email | `profile.email` | *(empty)* |  |
| Phone | `profile.phone` | *(empty)* |  |
| LinkedIn URL | `profile.linkedin` | *(empty)* |  |
| GitHub URL | `profile.github` | *(empty)* |  |
| Location | `profile.location` | `Almere, Netherlands` |  |
| Years of experience | `profile.years_experience` | `3` |  Allowed: 0-40. |
| Short pitch (for application forms) | `profile.pitch` | `built-in text` | 2-3 sentences, shown on the 'My snippets' page for forms that ask for a summary. |
| Your current job title | `profile.job_title` | `Medior Software Engineer` | Used as 'As a <title> at <employer>...'. |
| Your current employer | `profile.employer` | `GS1 Nederland` |  |
| Your ambition | `profile.ambition` | `built-in text` | The heart of every letter: where you want to grow and what kind of work you want to do more of, in your own words (1-2 sentences, first person). Specific beats grand: 'I want to own the design of high-traffic payment services' says more than 'I want to grow'. |
| Your ambition in Dutch (optional) | `profile.ambition_nl` | `built-in text` | Used when a letter is written in Dutch. Empty = the English text is used. |
| Concrete achievements | `profile.achievements` | `performance, scale, C#, SQL, Azure :: I drove a major per...` | One per line:  tags :: English sentence \|\| Nederlandse zin  (the Dutch part is optional). Tags are the skills and topics involved, e.g.  API design, REST, C#, Azure :: I led the development of ... Each letter uses the two achievements that overlap most with the posting, in your own words, and only names skills that appear in their tags. Use real numbers and outcomes: they are what makes a letter specific. |
| Letter language | `profile.letter_language` | `auto` |  |
| CV text | `profile.cv_text` | *(empty)* | Read from the file you upload above; edit it freely (fix odd line breaks, remove what you'd rather not share). It is sent to your AI agent only when you press 'Agent Customize' on a job, and never anywhere else. |
| Skills and weights | `profile.skills` | `C#: 3, .NET: 3, ASP.NET: 2, Azure: 3, Python: 2, SQL: 2, ...` | One per line as  Skill: weight  (weight 1 = nice to have, 2 = solid, 3 = your core stack). Matched against the job title and description. Letters only say you USE skills weighted 2 or 3. |

## Matching: countries, pay, experience

What counts as a job worth showing. Jobs that fail these rules are not saved at all.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Countries to search | `search.countries` | `['NL']` | Tick one or more. Every source searches all ticked countries (LinkedIn once per country), and the Jobs page gets a country filter. More countries = more requests = a slower refresh. Company feeds are filtered by each job's location; 'Any other site' (browser) entries use the country in their own address, so add one per country. |
| Include remote jobs | `search.include_remote` | `off` | Off = only jobs located in the ticked countries. On = also keep jobs whose location says 'Remote' (from any country). |
| Extra place words (optional) | `search.country_keywords` | *(empty)* | One per line. Extra words that also count as 'in one of my countries', e.g. a small town. The main cities and names of every country are already built in. |
| Minimum pay per country | `search.pay_by_country` | `{'NL': {'min': 90000, 'big': 70000}}` | One row per country you search, in that country's own currency, yearly gross. <b>Minimum</b>: postings that STATE less are dropped (when no salary is stated, pay is estimated instead, see 'Pay lookups'). <b>Big companies</b>: the lower minimum for companies you marked as 'big' on the Companies page: for them any job title may pay somewhat less, because of the career potential. Monthly salaries are converted to yearly first (see 'How salaries are calculated'). |
| Which company tiers count as 'big' | `search.big_company_tiers` | `[1]` | A company's tier is set on the Companies page. LinkedIn jobs from companies you haven't added there are never treated as big. Untick all to turn the lower big-company minimum off. |
| Show jobs whose pay I couldn't find | `search.show_unknown_pay` | `on` | Most postings state no salary and a web search doesn't always find one. On (recommended): such jobs are listed, marked 'pay unknown' and ranked a little lower, because your minimum only applies when a salary is known. Off: they are hidden until a pay estimate is found. |
| Holiday pay added to monthly salaries | `search.vacation_allowance_pct` | `8` | Monthly gross x 12, plus this holiday allowance (Dutch vakantiegeld is 8 %), unless the posting says it is already included. Set 0 to turn off. Unit: %. Allowed: 0-20. |
| Add stated bonuses | `search.add_bonus` | `on` | Adds a bonus the posting actually states (e.g. '10% bonus', 'bonus of €5.000', '13th month'). One-off sign-on or relocation money is never added, and nothing is added when no bonus is stated. |
| Maximum years of experience asked | `search.max_years_required` | `4` | Postings that ask for more years of experience than this are dropped. Title words like 'Senior', 'Staff', 'Lead' are filtered separately (see Advanced). Unit: years. Allowed: 0-20. |
| Ignore postings older than | `search.max_age_days` | `60` |  Unit: days. Allowed: 1-365. |
| Treat a re-posted role as new after | `search.repost_gap_days` | `30` | Companies re-open the same role for a new batch. A posting with the same title and company that appears more than this many days after the one already saved counts as a NEW opening and is checked again. A new posting ID always counts as new. Older postings are never re-fetched. Unit: days. Allowed: 1-365. |

## LinkedIn search

LinkedIn's public (logged-out) job search, used to find jobs at companies that aren't on your Companies list. It searches each country ticked in Settings → Matching separately. It never uses your LinkedIn account. LinkedIn's terms forbid scraping, so keep volume low.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Search LinkedIn | `linkedin.enabled` | `on` |  |
| Search terms | `linkedin.queries` | `software engineer, junior software engineer, junior devel...` | One per line. Each is searched separately, so more terms = more requests = slower. |
| LinkedIn experience levels | `linkedin.experience_levels` | `[2, 3, 4]` |  |
| Only jobs posted in the last | `linkedin.window_days` | `7` |  Unit: days. Allowed: 1-30. |
| Result pages per search term | `linkedin.pages_per_query` | `3` | 25 jobs per page. Allowed: 1-10. |
| Pause between requests | `linkedin.delay_seconds` | `3` | Keep this at 2 seconds or more to stay polite. The scraper stops by itself if LinkedIn pushes back. Unit: seconds. Allowed: 1-30. |

## Pay lookups (when a job doesn't state a salary)

Most postings don't show a salary. For those, the app looks up what is typically paid for that company and level: first the reported-pay table, then a quick web search of Glassdoor / Levels.fyi / Indeed result snippets, and for big companies it may assume.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Search the web for typical pay | `salary.online_lookup` | `on` | Free, no account needed. Results are cached so only a few searches happen per run. |
| Max web searches per scrape | `salary.max_lookups_per_run` | `20` |  Allowed: 0-200. |
| Remember results for | `salary.cache_days` | `45` |  Unit: days. Allowed: 1-365. |
| Pause between searches | `salary.delay_seconds` | `3.0` |  Unit: seconds. Allowed: 0-30. |
| Your own pay data | `salary.benchmarks` | *(empty)* | Overrides everything else. One per line:  Company \| junior or medior \| low \| high  (yearly €, e.g.  Mollie \| medior \| 75000 \| 95000 ). |

## AI agent (optional)

Lets an AI model write a fully customised motivation letter for a job: press <b>Agent Customize</b> on a job page and the letter box is filled with the result for you to check. Works with Claude, with any OpenAI-compatible service, or with a model running on your own hardware (Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, vLLM...). <b>What is sent:</b> only when you press that button, the job posting, your profile, achievements and CV text go to the endpoint you configure below. Nothing is sent otherwise. <b>Cost:</b> hosted services bill per use (typically a few cents per letter), so set a spending limit; a model on your own network is free.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enable the AI agent | `ai.enabled` | `off` | Adds the Agent Customize button to every job page (needs the details below). |
| Type of service | `ai.provider` | `anthropic` | Almost every other service and local model server speaks the OpenAI-compatible protocol. |
| Server address | `ai.base_url` | *(empty)* | The address up to and including <code>/v1</code>; the app adds <code>/chat/completions</code>. Ollama: <code>http://host:11434/v1</code>. OpenAI: <code>https://api.openai.com/v1</code>. Inside Docker, <code>localhost</code> is the container itself: use the machine's LAN address instead. |
| API key | `ai.api_key` | *(empty)* | Stored in this app's database on your own drive, never shown again and never included in any page. Optional for models on your own network. Prefer not to store it? Leave this empty and set the JOBHUNTER_AI_API_KEY environment variable instead (docker: in your .env file). Leave the box empty to keep the saved key. |
| Model | `ai.model` | *(empty)* | Claude: leave empty for the most capable model, or e.g. <code>claude-sonnet-5-5</code> for cheaper. OpenAI-compatible: required, the model name as the server knows it (e.g. <code>llama3.1:8b</code>). |
| Give up after | `ai.timeout_seconds` | `180` | Small models on a Raspberry Pi can be slow; raise this if letters time out. Unit: seconds. Allowed: 30-1800. |

## Schedule

How the app keeps jobs fresh by itself, quietly in the background. You can always press 'Scrape now' to refresh everything immediately.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Refresh jobs automatically | `schedule.enabled` | `on` |  |
| Refresh every company once every | `schedule.every_hours` | `24` | A full refresh once a day (24) is plenty: job boards rarely change faster than that. Unit: hours. Allowed: 1-168. |
| Spread the work evenly | `schedule.spread` | `on` | On (recommended): one company at a time, spread over the whole period. With 22 companies and 24 hours that is one every ~65 minutes, so the machine is never busy for long. Off: everything is refreshed in one go when the period is up. |
| Run at lowest CPU priority | `schedule.low_priority` | `on` | Recommended when the machine also does other work (media server, Pi-hole, ...). Scraping then only uses CPU that nothing else wants. It just takes longer. |
| Rest between companies | `schedule.pause_between_sources` | `15` | Spreads the work out so it never runs as one big burst. Unit: seconds. Allowed: 0-600. |
| Pause between page requests | `schedule.pause_between_requests` | `0.5` |  Unit: seconds. Allowed: 0-10. |

## Advanced: title rules & browser

Regular expressions (case-insensitive, one per line) that decide which job titles are considered. You usually don't need to change these; the defaults are tuned for junior/medior software roles.

| Setting | Path | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|---|
| Title must match one of | `search.title_include` | `software, developer, engineer, ontwikkelaar, programmeur,...` | Jobs whose title matches none of these are not software roles. |
| Skip titles matching | `search.title_exclude` | `\bintern(ship)?\b, stagiair, werkstudent, apprentice, the...` | Interns, sales engineers, hardware roles, managers, ... |
| Skip titles that are too senior | `search.title_too_senior` | `\bsenior\b, \bsr\b, \bstaff\b, \bprincipal\b, \blead\b, \...` | Senior, staff, principal, lead, architect, 'Engineer III', ... |
| Title marks a junior role | `search.title_junior_markers` | `\bjunior\b, \bjr\b, \bentry\b, \bgraduate\b, \bassociate\...` |  |
| Title marks a medior role | `search.title_medior_markers` | `\bmedior\b, \bmid[- ]?level\b, \bmid\b, \bintermediate\b,...` |  |
| Exchange rates to euro | `search.fx_to_eur` | `GBP: 1.15, CHF: 1.05, SEK: 0.09, DKK: 0.134, NOK: 0.087, ...` | Salaries in other currencies are converted with these rates so they can be compared with your minimum. One per line as  GBP: 1.15  (1 unit of that currency in euro). Approximate is fine. |
| Browser program (optional) | `browser.executable` | *(empty)* | Path to Chromium, e.g. /usr/bin/chromium on a Raspberry Pi. Empty = Playwright's own download. |
| Pause between page loads | `browser.delay_seconds` | `2` |  Unit: seconds. Allowed: 0-30. |

## Companies

Managed on the **Companies** page. Each entry has a name, a **tier** (1 = big / high-paying, 2 = decent) and a career-site type with its own details:

| Type | Fields | Where to find them |
|---|---|---|
| Greenhouse (`greenhouse`) | `board`* | Open the company's job board; the address looks like boards.greenhouse.io/**board** or job-boards.greenhouse.io/**board**. |
| Lever (`lever`) | `site`*, `eu` | Address looks like jobs.lever.co/**site**. European customers may use jobs.eu.lever.co. |
| Ashby (`ashby`) | `board`* | Address looks like jobs.ashbyhq.com/**board**. |
| SmartRecruiters (`smartrecruiters`) | `company_id`* | Address looks like jobs.smartrecruiters.com/**CompanyId**. |
| Workday (`workday`) | `tenant`*, `wd`*, `site`*, `search` | Address looks like **tenant**.**wd5**.myworkdayjobs.com/**site**/... - copy the three parts. |
| Jibe / iCIMS career site (`jibe`) | `host`*, `keywords` | Career sites such as jobs.booking.com whose search results come from /api/jobs. |
| Amazon (own site) (`amazon`) | none | Built in - nothing to fill in. |
| Uber (own site) (`uber`) | none | Built in - nothing to fill in. |
| Any other site (browser) (`browser`) | `url`*, `link_pattern`*, `next`, `max_pages` | For sites without a feed. Search on the site with your filters, copy the results-page address, then open any job and copy what its address has in common (e.g. `/jobs/\d+`). Needs the optional browser install (see the Help page). |

`*` = required. A company can be paused without deleting it.

## Only in `config.yaml`

| Key | Default | Why it isn't in the UI |
|---|---|---|
| `web.host` | `0.0.0.0` | changing the address from the page you're using could lock you out; needs a restart |
| `web.port` | `8585` | same; pick a port nothing else (e.g. Pi-hole) uses |
| `db_path` | `data/jobs.db` | where the database lives; it holds the settings themselves |
| `manual_links` | list | quick links on the Status page; rarely changed |
